name: MCP tools auth timeouts isolation
short_definition: Model Context Protocol (MCP) exposes tools to LLMs/agents with explicit schemas, auth, timeouts, and isolation. Production Python servers use the official mcp package (FastMCP in SDK) and/or standalone fastmcp for streamable HTTP; fastapi-mcp bridges existing FastAPI routes. Never treat MCP as unauthenticated stdio on a shared host without sandboxing. As of 2026-07-13: mcp 1.28.1, fastapi-mcp 0.4.0. Tools MUST validate inputs, enforce authZ, bound runtime, and sanitize outputs.
scope_in: Python server options: mcp SDK FastMCP, standalone fastmcp, fastapi-mcp
Transports: stdio (local), streamable HTTP (remote default), legacy SSE notes
Auth: OAuth 2.1 / bearer / API key for remote; dependency injection for FastAPI bridges
Timeouts, rate limits, output size limits, human-in-the-loop for destructive ops
Process/network isolation and least-privilege credentials for tool backends
scope_out: Temporal durable orchestration of multi-step agents (py-durable-workflows)
Client IDE plugin development (Claude Desktop config minutiae beyond auth headers)

defaults.server: Official mcp Python SDK FastMCP for new tool servers; fastapi-mcp when reusing existing FastAPI routes+Depends auth
defaults.remote_transport: streamable-http (not raw public stdio); mount under /mcp behind auth
defaults.local_dev: stdio OK for single-user desktop agents with trusted tools only
defaults.auth_remote: OAuth 2.1 or service bearer tokens; reject anonymous remote tools
defaults.schemas: Pydantic/JSON Schema inputSchema (and outputSchema when structured); no dict[str, Any] free-for-all
defaults.timeouts: Per-tool timeout (e.g. 5–30s default; explicit higher for long jobs with async handle pattern)
defaults.limits: Rate limit tools/call; max response bytes; max concurrent calls per principal
defaults.destructive: annotations + client confirmation; server-side authZ still mandatory
defaults.isolation: Separate process/container; least-privilege DB/API credentials; no host shell by default

use_mcp_when: Exposing capabilities to multiple agent hosts (Claude, IDE, internal agents) with standard discovery
Need typed tool catalog separate from product REST API
use_fastapi_rest_only_when: Only first-party app calls tools via your HTTP API — MCP optional
Strict OpenAPI BFF already covers all clients
use_fastapi_mcp_when: Existing FastAPI endpoints should become tools without rewrite
do_not: Don't expose production DB shell tools over unauthenticated MCP
Don't run untrusted MCP servers with full filesystem/network in CI agents without sandbox
Don't rely on tool annotations alone for security (untrusted unless server trusted)

do: AuthN before tools/call; authZ per tool and resource
Set client and server timeouts; return isError on tool failure
Log tool name, principal, duration, success — not secrets
Design tools as goals/capabilities, not raw internal REST dumps
Sandbox outbound network (SSRF allowlists) for fetch-like tools
dont: Don't allow arbitrary SQL/shell tools in multi-tenant prod
Don't return multi-MB blobs into LLM context
Don't skip human confirm on payments, deletes, transfers
Don't share one credential for all tenants inside a tool
Don't block forever on upstream APIs without timeout
Don't mount MCP on public internet without TLS + auth

code_skeleton:
# --- FastMCP (mcp SDK) tool server ---
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

mcp = FastMCP("orders-tools")

class OrderQuery(BaseModel):
    order_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)

@mcp.tool()
async def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Return status for an order the caller is allowed to see."""
    # enforce auth from context/headers in HTTP mode; validate ownership
    if not order_id:
        return "error: missing order_id"
    return f"order {order_id}: shipped"  # real DB call with tenant check

# Remote: mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
# Local:  mcp.run()  # stdio

# --- fastapi-mcp bridge sketch ---
# from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
# from fastapi_mcp import FastApiMCP
# app = FastAPI()
# @app.get("/orders/{order_id}")
# async def get_order(order_id: str, user=Depends(auth)):
#     ...
# FastApiMCP(app).mount()

# --- Client-side timeout policy (agent host) ---
# MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS=30000
# On timeout: cancel, record failure, do not retry destructive tools without idempotency key
failure_modes: Tool hangs → agent session timeout cascade
Unauthenticated remote MCP → data breach / RCE via tools
Prompt injection tricks model into calling destructive tools
Huge tool result floods context window (DoS)
Schema drift between server and clients after deploy
SSE/streamable HTTP proxy buffering breaks transport
Confused deputy: tool uses server's superuser credentials for attacker-controlled args
anti_patterns: MCP server with shell=True / unrestricted code exec
Auth only on HTTP middleware but tools bypass with internal calls
Returning raw exception stacks with secrets
Registering every internal REST route as a tool without curation
Trusting client-supplied tenant_id without server verification

versions_as_of.note: FastMCP 1.x lives in official mcp package; standalone fastmcp package evolves faster (v2/v3 features, OAuth helpers) — pick one stack and pin

deprecation_watch: Unauthenticated remote SSE MCP as default
Exposing all OpenAPI routes as tools without review
Ignoring MCP security guidance (human-in-the-loop for destructive tools)
Custom non-schema tool args (free-form strings only)
ts_boundary: TS/Next agents may host MCP clients or call your Python MCP over HTTP. Prefer server-side MCP client in BFF/agent worker — not browser direct to privileged tools. Product REST can remain separate from MCP tool surface; don't force browsers to speak MCP.
rust_boundary: High-assurance sandboxes or ultra-low-latency tool runtimes may be Rust; keep MCP schema contract stable. Default tool business logic stays Python when it touches AI/data stack.
supabase_boundary: Tools that read/write Supabase must use service credentials with explicit tenant checks, or user-scoped JWT passed carefully (no key leak into logs). Prefer dedicated RPC/SQL functions over open table access. RLS is not a substitute for tool authZ when using service_role.
boundary_contracts: MCP tools/list JSON Schema inputSchema (+ outputSchema optional)
Auth: OAuth bearer or API key on remote transport
Timeout and rate-limit SLOs documented per tool
Env for transport and tool secrets
OpenAPI remains separate for product HTTP; MCP is agent-facing contract

decision_matrix_row.ts: MCP client in server agent; UI confirms destructive ops
decision_matrix_row.rust: Optional sandbox executor behind same MCP schema

threats: RCE via unsafe tools (shell, eval, pickle)
Data exfiltration tools (email send, arbitrary HTTP)
DoS via slow or huge tool results
Token theft on remote MCP endpoints
mitigations: Allowlist tools; no generic code execution in prod
Pin mcp dependency; review third-party MCP servers before install

must_generate: Auth on remote MCP or documented local-only stdio
Minimal curated tool set — not entire API dump
must_not_generate: Unauthenticated public MCP with DB/shell tools
Logging of Authorization headers or raw secrets
Trusting annotations as sole security control

tests_required: tools/call validation errors for bad args
Timeout test with slow mock upstream
ci_gates: Grep ban for shell=True in mcp tool modules
skill_module_bullets: MCP tools are model-controlled — authZ, timeouts, isolation mandatory
Python: mcp FastMCP default; fastapi-mcp to reuse FastAPI Depends auth
Remote: streamable HTTP + OAuth/bearer; stdio only trusted local
Per-tool timeout, rate limit, output size cap
Human-in-the-loop for destructive tools; don't trust annotations alone
Curate tools as capabilities; validate schemas; tenant checks
